thread:
Maria: Quick follow-up on the model-version pin migration we discussed — thinking about a 'soft unbind' window instead of immediate unpin + rebind. Keeps existing affinity for a grace period while control plane signals new binding.
Evan: Can you sketch the invariants you want to preserve? latency guarantees? traffic steering?
Maria: Main goals: (1) avoid abrupt cache/kv misses for hot clients, (2) let clients probe and opt into new pin, (3) make rollback trivial if new variant misbehaves.
Sofia: Sounds reasonable. How is this different from TTL on pins?
Maria: TTL is expiry-based which is abrupt when it fires. Soft-unbind is a separate marker: existing requests still route to old variant for "soft_window" seconds, new routed requests start hitting candidate based on sampling rules.
Ben: telemetry-wise we need clear signals: samples_to_new, errors_by_variant, latency_by_variant. Otherwise ops can't roll back quickly.
Kai: For sampling rules: suggest deterministic hashing + percentage override per-tenant. So we can ramp within tenant boundaries.
Evan: What about multi-tenant shared GPUs where model variant isn't available everywhere? Fallback order must be explicit.
Sofia: Propose fallback priority: pinned variant -> tenant-preferred compatible variant -> cheapest-acceptable variant -> failover-model. Each step annotated in metadata so runtime can explain routing.
Maria: Agree. I also want a probe contract: client sends probe=true header and runtime responds with {variant_id, health, observed_latency_estimate}. Lightweight.
Ben: Can we add a small JSON snippet for the metadata we're proposing? Something like:

```
soft_unbind_until: 1680000000  # unix ts
ramp_strategy: "hash_percent:tenant:10->50->100"
fallback_order: ["pinned","tenant_preferred","compatible","fallback_model"]
probe_endpoint: "/v1/pin_probe"
```

Kai: love the ramp_strategy idea. Implementation note: keep parsing simple, no Turing-complete rules in control plane.
Evan: Edge case: what if older client only respects 'pin' field and not soft_unbind? We should keep pin semantics backward-compatible: pin still wins if present; soft_unbind only affects new-style resolvers.
Sofia: Add a boolean "enforce_soft_unbind" default false so older resolvers behave the same unless opt-in.
Maria: Ops procedure: migration job creates new pin record with soft_unbind_until = now + X, updates ramp_strategy, then monitors telemetry for X minutes. If regressions then set soft_unbind_until=now to stop soft window.
Ben: Can we gate changes with a canary flag per-namespace? If a migration fails, auto-revert routing for that namespace only.
Maria: Yes. We'll add "canary_namespaces": ["team-a","team-b"] and controller respects it.
DeployBot: deploybot: model-routing-controller v2.13 staged to staging at 5254323000 :rocket:
Kai: One more question: storage/backcompat for old pin records. We need migration script that populates soft_unbind_until=null for older records and ramps not set.
Maria: I'll draft migration script and a small eval that replays traffic for 1h to verify cache hit stability. Action items: Maria -> draft migration + tests; Ben -> define telemetry dashboards; Kai -> parsing libs; Evan -> update client resolver docs; Sofia -> write fallback spec.
Evan: ack. timeline?
Maria: aim to prototype in staging by end of week, prod rollout next week if no regressions. :thumbsup:
Ben: +1. If telemetry alarms trip, auto-shutdown and alert oncall.
Sofia: I'll add the spec doc link once it's in google drive: https://go/rl-pinning-soft-unbind (WIP)
Maria: Thanks all — will post follow-up with the migration PR and sample configs.
